meta.originalInput: You don't leave social gatherings tired because you talked too much. You leave exhausted because you were holding a mask. When you perform for others, your natural personal perimeter contracts under constant external pressure. The perimeter shrinks inward. The walls thin. Maintaining that perimeter consumes every ounce of cognitive reserve. Solitude isn't about hiding. It's the only place your natural boundary can finally expand back to full size.
